stem: Johnny is a 10-year-old boy who has had a high-speed bicycle collision and is described as semi-conscious. After assessing airway, breathing and circulation, you move on to a rapid neurological assessment. Which one of the following is a useful initial approach to assess Johnny's neurological status?

options.text: Shake the patient by the head

explanation: A rapid initial neurological assessment begins with assessing conscious level using a simple voice response, such as asking the child if they are alright, followed by escalation to AVPU/GCS and pupillary assessment as needed. Painful stimulus is reserved for a more formal assessment of responsiveness and should be used carefully; shaking the head is inappropriate, and deep tendon reflexes are not part of the initial trauma neurological assessment.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: The question asks for an initial bedside method to assess conscious level in a head-injured child; speaking to the patient is the least invasive first step.

optionExplanations.A: Appropriate first step to assess conscious level and responsiveness.
optionExplanations.B: May be used later in a structured assessment, but not the best initial approach.
optionExplanations.C: Unsafe and inappropriate in suspected head injury.
optionExplanations.D: Not part of the rapid initial assessment of neurological status.

source.questionTextHtml:
Happy with ABC, you move on to rapidly assess D. Rapid clinical assessment of neurologic status consists of establishing conscious level and pupillary responses.

Which one of the following is a useful initial approach to assess Johnny’s neurologic status?

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
